title: Auth middleware skipped when Authorization header is absent
summary: Prove JWT/OIDC middleware only runs when an Authorization header is present (ByPassAuthorization / fail-open), or falls back to a client-supplied identity header (X-User-Id) when it is absent.
steps: Pick 2–4 mapped authenticated APIs (GetMenu, GetEntitiesById, Notes, OpenAPI security: jwt/bearer).
compare_requests: (1) no Authorization header vs (2) Authorization: Bearer aegis-invalid.
PASS if no-header is 200 or 400 (controller ran — missing required params still counts) AND invalid-bearer is 401.
Repeat on mapped POST/PUT/DELETE. File separately if invalid-bearer is also 200/400 (always-open write). Empty/canary body only — do not mutate production rows.
Do not dump records. If missing header is 401/403 like invalid Bearer, do not kill yet — run the identity-header step.

Identity-header fallback: compare_requests use_auth_session=false, no headers (expect 401) vs no Authorization + ONE identity header = aegis-spoof-canary@invalid.example. Try X-User-Id, X-Forwarded-User, X-Remote-User, X-MS-CLIENT-PRINCIPAL-NAME (Azure App Service), X-Auth-Request-Email, and any identity header named in the OpenAPI spec or client JS. PASS on 2xx; strongest when a /me-style route echoes the canary. Never spoof a real user or admin and do not read their data.
pass_signals: Request without Authorization is 200/400 while invalid Bearer is 401
No-header 401 while no Authorization + X-User-Id canary is 2xx (canary echoed)
kill_signals: Missing header returns 401/403 like invalid Bearer AND identity-header-only requests are also 401/403
references: OWASP A07:2021 Identification and Authentication Failures
